summary: HF-01S is an interactive lunar lander simulator designed to help users understand the challenges of landing a spacecraft on the Moon. The project provides a browser-based simulation where users can control a lunar lander and explore the effects of thrust, velocity, fuel consumption, and landing conditions. It aims to make lunar landing concepts more accessible through hands-on experimentation and interactive learning. By combining simulation technology with an educational experience, HF-01S encourages users to explore spacecraft control, landing safety, and the complexity of lunar exploration.
details:
HF-01S: Lunar Landing Simulator is an offline-capable, browser-based 2D scientific lunar landing simulator designed to help students and junior operators understand the challenges of powered descent and precision landing on the Moon.

The simulator recreates a lunar landing mission at Mare Tranquillitatis (TQ-01), using a fixed-timestep Newtonian physics engine and lunar gravity of 1.62 m/s². Users can control the spacecraft through three operational modes: Training, Assisted, and Manual. Each mode provides different levels of guidance and control difficulty.

The system includes a Mission Control interface, pre-flight briefing, real-time flight deck, telemetry monitoring, propulsion and subsystem indicators, terrain hazard detection, and post-flight debriefing. Users must manage thrust, velocity, attitude, propellant consumption, and spacecraft stability to achieve a safe touchdown.

The project provides an interactive STEM learning experience by transforming aerospace physics concepts into practical simulation exercises. It encourages problem-solving, critical thinking, engineering awareness, and systems management.

HF-01S was developed as a lightweight, zero-dependency web application that can run locally in a modern browser without requiring complex installation or continuous internet access. The project also includes automated testing using Node.js to validate physics calculations, subsystem behavior, and user interface workflows.

Its creativity lies in combining realistic flight-control concepts, progressive training modes, dynamic subsystem failures, and mission debriefing into an accessible educational lunar landing simulator.
